title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: an abstract 'inégalité' M, Grothendieck's axiomatic stand-in for a space of closed cells. It is a set with a partial order ≤ ('is a face of'), a relation ≪ (marked with a small circle, roughly 'lies in the interior / strictly below'), a relation |·| ('meet properly / are in general position'), and derived relations. One derived relation is a compatibility relation, written as a crossed comparison sign and transcribed as ≴. By the next page it means 'X and Y belong to a common figure'. Another is ∥. A figure F ⊂ M is a downward-closed subset whose elements are pairwise compatible: an abstract cell complex inside M. For X in M, X̃ = M_{≤X} is the set of faces of X.

Previous page: a figure indexed by a poset I is an increasing map φ: I → M. The proposition there says φ defines such a figure iff (a) φ is increasing and injective; (b) for each i, φ restricts to an order isomorphism I_{≤i} ≅ X̃_i, where X_i = φ(i); (c) for i, j incomparable in I (the '|·|' of the trivial structure on I), X_i |·| X_j.

This page finishes the sufficiency proof.
- Condition (b) already makes φ(I) downward closed.
- It remains to show X_i and X_j are compatible for all i, j. Compatibility is unpacked as: for every X' in X̃_i minus X̃_i∩X̃_j and every Y' in X̃_j minus X̃_i∩X̃_j, X' |·| Y'.
- By (b), X' = X_{i'} with i' ≤ i, and Y' = X_{j'} with j' ≤ j. Since X' ≠ Y', also i' ≠ j'.
- Condition (c) then gives X_{i'} |·| X_{j'}. QED.

Next comes a short 'polyhedral variant'. When the ambient structure is polyhedral, one restricts to polyhedral figures. He says this costs nothing, because polyhedrality of a figure can be read off its parts. The text here is partly illegible.

Then a first definition of morphisms of inégalités φ: M → M': (a) preserve ≤; (b) preserve ≪̊; (c) preserve |·|. A bracket announces a further condition (d) 'plus loin'.

Grothendieck then weighs the definition:
- He asks whether this is too demanding, and judges it reasonable for embeddings of inégalités.
- He considers also requiring that compatibility be preserved, but notes this is again demanding.
- He records that ≪ is preserved, while preservation of compatibility and of ∥ is left as a question.
- NB: if M is the trivial inégalité, the conditions force φ to be injective.

The next page resolves the question by adding (d): φ induces a bijection X̃ → φ(X)~ on face sets. Under (a), (c), (d), images of figures are figures and compatibility is preserved. The whole project serves Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at an axiomatic 'tame' or polyhedral topology, in which spaces are handled through posets of cells and their incidence relations.
errors: Small gap in the final step. Condition (c) applies to incomparable indices, but Grothendieck only records i' ≠ j'. The missing step is easy: if i' ≤ j', then X' = X_{i'} ≤ X_{j'} ≤ X_j, so X' would lie in X̃_j, contradicting the choice of X'. The symmetric case is the same, so i' and j' are incomparable and (c) applies.
The text writes 'pour i,j ∈ F' where 'i,j ∈ I' is meant.
The relation to be proved is the compatibility relation ('belong to a common figure'), not the order relation ≰ as the transcription renders it.

ideas.what: Characterisation of 'figures indexed by a poset I' (abstract cell complexes inside an incidence structure M). The conditions are: injective, increasing, an isomorphism on each down-set, and incomparable indices sent to properly-meeting cells.
ideas.modern_name: Face poset of a regular cell complex; realisation of an abstract cell complex in an ambient incidence structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tucker (abstract cell complexes, 1933); Björner (CW posets, 1984); abstract polytopes (Danzer–Schulte)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (1984), without these axiomatics

ideas.what: Definition of morphisms of 'inégalités': maps preserving ≤, ≪ and |·|, later adding the requirement of a bijection on face sets.
ideas.modern_name: Cellular maps that are isomorphisms on closed cells (dimension-preserving, non-degenerate maps of face posets; local isomorphisms of down-sets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in combinatorial topology (simplicial maps injective on simplices, morphisms of regular CW complexes)

ideas.what: The 'polyhedral variant': restricting to polyhedral figures, with polyhedrality read off the parts of a figure.

missed.claim: The page is part of an unpublished axiomatisation ('inégalités', figures, relations ≤, ≪, |·|, compatibility, ∥) for tame or polyhedral topology. Its morphism notion is explicitly left open: Grothendieck asks whether it is too demanding, and a 17.7.86 note on the next page says condition (d) should be weakened. This axiomatic incidence-structure approach to tame topology does not appear in the literature as a completed framework.
missed.quote: (Est-ce trop exigeant ??) Ça semble raisonnable dans le cas d'un plongement des inégalités
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with o-minimal cell decompositions, CW posets and exit-path/stratified approaches. However, the content on this page is elementary combinatorics and adds little by itself.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine combinatorial lemma and a tentative morphism definition. The only interest is that it documents the little-known 1986 axiomatic 'Analysis situs' framework.
transcription_corrections: 'En effet, b) implique déjà que φ(…) est fermée' should read 'φ(I) est fermée'.
The symbol transcribed '≴' / '≇' in 'X_i ≴ X_j', in 'X ≴ Y ⇏ X' ≴ Y'' and in the last lines is the compatibility sign (a crossed ≶-type symbol, 'belong to a common figure'), not '≰'.
'C'est-ce trop exigeant ??' should read 'Est-ce trop exigeant ??'.
'dans le cas d'une plongement des inégalités' should read 'dans le cas d'un plongement des inégalités'.
The bracket after c) likely reads '[+ d) plus loin importante]'.
'l'espace vectoriel I polyédral' is doubtful from the image; context suggests the ambient structure (or I) being polyhedral, not a vector space.
The heading 'Variantes polyédrales' replaces a struck-out 'Morphismes de …'.
The NB likely reads 'Si M est une inégalité triviale, ces conditions impliquent que φ injective'.
